captions.text: Hi, this is Nobikos. Ask me what I can do for your team.

Hi there. Nobikos keeps the reasoning behind decisions, not just the facts. When your team uses AI to write code or draft text, we capture the moments where a person actually thinks it through, corrects the AI, or explains why something matters. We store that with the person's name and their reason in their own words. So when someone asks who knows something, they get a real colleague and why they know it, instead of just asking how it was done. It's less about asking how, more about talking why.
What would my team actually use it for?

Let me give you two quick ones. First, your people can ask in Slack or through an AI assistant "who knows this topic" and get back the colleague who actually worked it out, with their reason in their own words, and a way to chat with them. That's live today. Second, you as a leader can see which topics are going dark,  where only one person knows something, or nobody has explained it lately. That's live too, and it helps you spot where knowledge is at risk before someone leaves. What matters most to your team right now?
And as a manager, what do I get?

As a manager, you see where knowledge is at risk. We show you topics that only one person understands, or nobody has reasoned about in a while, we call that going dark. You get the topic names, never who knows what, so there's no scoring people. It helps you plan handovers and spot gaps before they become problems when someone leaves or moves to a new role.
Is the onboarding path live already?

No, that's on the roadmap. Right now we have who knows and going dark live for you. The onboarding path,  building a learning route around what a newcomer already knows, that's an idea we're working toward, not built yet.
You're welcome. Feel free to reach out anytime you want to know more. Take care.
